title: Silky Hummus with Tahini, Lemon and Cumin
summary: Canned chickpeas are simmered soft and skinned, then blended with a strained garlic-lemon liquid, cumin, plenty of tahini and olive oil, and served with warm pita.

ingredients.item: x 400 g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed
garlic cloves, grated to a paste
fine sea salt or table salt
pita breads, warmed and cut into wedges

steps.title: Simmer the chickpeas
steps.text: Put the chickpeas, bicarbonate of soda and 1.5 litres water in the pan. Bring to the boil and simmer 20-25 minutes until very soft and the skins float.

steps.title: Infuse the lemon
steps.text: Stir the garlic, lemon juice and salt in a small bowl and leave 10 minutes. Strain, pressing on the garlic, and discard the solids.

steps.title: Remove the skins
steps.text: Drain the chickpeas, return to the pan and cover with cold water. Swish with your fingers and pour off the floating skins; repeat 3-4 times. Drain and keep 2 tbsp whole chickpeas aside.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the remaining chickpeas with the lemon liquid, 60 ml cold water and the cumin for 1 minute. Add the tahini and 2 tbsp oil and blend 1 minute more until pale and creamy, adding water a teaspoon at a time if it is too thick.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spread in a shallow bowl and top with the reserved chickpeas, a pinch of cumin, parsley and a drizzle of oil. Serve with warm pita.

tips: Removing the skins is what makes this hummus so silky.
Straining the garlic gives its flavour without harsh raw bits.
The hummus thickens as it chills; loosen with a spoonful of water before serving.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 4 days. Do not leave out for more than 2 hours. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
